findings.issue: M2(a) is two claims welded together with an 'and', and they have opposite novelty profiles. Fragment (a1) is a PHYSICS claim: the divergent system's Hough eigenfrequencies depart from -2Ω/[n(n+1)] by a quantified amount at Earth's ε (40% at m=1,n=2; 28% at n=3; 13% at n=5; 6% at n=8). Fragment (a2) is a VERIFICATION-PRACTICE claim: the solver is checked against a closed-form ε→0 limit the project derives itself rather than against a published table. (a1) has heavy prior art (see F15). (a2) has no physics novelty at all — asymptotic-limit code verification is routine — and its real function in the contract is rhetorical cover for the fact that Longuet-Higgins (1968) and Swarztrauber & Kasahara (1985) could not be obtained. A referee who owns those papers will read 'rather than against a published table' as 'the authors did not check against the published tables'. Bundled, the weak fragment inherits the strong fragment's protection and neither gets challenged properly in Step 11.
findings.evidence: SCOPE_CONTRACT.md §M2(a); theory/derivations.tex §6.3 (sec:hough:limit) and §6.4; docs/CONVENTIONS.md 'Extension B validation — the ε → 0 limit and the missing references'; docs/literature/MISSING.md 'Genuinely unobtainable'.
findings.recommended_revision: Split M2 into M2(a1) and M2(a2). M2(a1): 'That the fractional slowing of each divergent Rossby-branch eigenfrequency relative to -2Ω/[n(n+1)] at Earth's ε ≈ 8.80 is quantified mode by mode, and that this quantification is shown to be either absent from, or consistent with, the classical Hough tabulations (Longuet-Higgins 1968; Kasahara 1976; Swarztrauber & Kasahara 1985).' M2(a2): 'That the eigenvalue solver is verified against the internally derived ε→0 closed form with a measured first-order convergence rate — stated as code verification, not as a scientific contribution, and not offered as a substitute for an external finite-ε benchmark.' Delete the phrase 'rather than against a published table' from the contract entirely; it is a defensive tell.

findings.issue: The internal validation target does not validate the regime the headline numbers come from, and structurally cannot test the operator that produces them. Two separate defects. (i) REGIME: check_hough_epsilon_limit.py fits the convergence rate over ε ∈ [1e-6, 1e-2], and the quantified departures are quoted at ε ≈ 8.80 — nearly three decades above the top of the fitted window. A first-order convergence exponent measured at ε ≤ 1e-2 says nothing about the coefficient, and nothing at all about a 40% slowing at ε = 8.80. (ii) STRUCTURE: the ε→0 limit is obtained by setting δ = η̃ = 0 in eq. (eq:houghevp), which leaves the diagonal system dζ_n/dτ = (im/Λ_n)ζ_n. That check exercises exactly one matrix entry. It cannot detect an error in the Coriolis coupling B = M - DΛ⁻¹ or in the Legendre matrices M and D — and B is precisely the operator that produces the departure being claimed. The validation is weakest exactly where the physics of interest lives.
findings.evidence: theory/derivations.tex §6.2 eq. (eq:houghevp) and eq. (eq:legmat); §6.3 'ε ∈ [10^{-6}, 10^{-2}]' and 'obtaining 1.0000 to four figures'; §6.4 'At ε ≈ 8.80 the correction is large'; SCOPE_CONTRACT.md §M2(a).
findings.recommended_revision: Add to M2(a2) an explicit second validation requirement: 'and that at least one finite-ε eigenfrequency in the range relevant to Earth (ε = O(1-10)) is cross-checked against an independently published value — Kasahara (1976), Swarztrauber & Kasahara (1985), the MODES/normal-mode-function literature, or an independent solver — because the ε→0 limit decouples the Coriolis coupling matrix B and therefore cannot verify it.' Promote obtaining Kasahara (1976) from MISSING.md's 'accessible substitutes to obtain' (where it currently sits as optional) to a hard campaign deliverable.

findings.issue: The single most defensible piece of new content in the entire theory is not named in the scope contract, so Step 11 will not challenge it and Step 16 will not check the bibliography against it. Theory §6.5 reports that sectoral modes (n = m) are slowed systematically less than their n = m+1 neighbours (7.5% against 19.8% at m=2), gives a structural cause (a sectoral mode sits at the bottom of the degree ladder and has one tridiagonal neighbour instead of two), and — unusually — demonstrates it CAUSALLY by deleting the lower neighbour of a non-sectoral mode from the basis and collapsing its slowing from 19.8% to 6.4% against a true sectoral 7.5%. That numerical-experiment-as-causal-test is the kind of thing a referee remembers. M2(a) as worded ('quantification of the departure ... from the nondivergent Rossby-Haurwitz prediction') does not cover it: a systematic family-dependent exception is not a quantification of a departure. It is also flagged in H5 as 'predicted, not a failure', so it is load-bearing for a hypothesis.
findings.evidence: theory/derivations.tex §6.5 (sec:hough:sectoral), including the basis-deletion experiment and the local-deformation-radius argument ε⟨sin²φ⟩/[n(n+1)]; §12 H5 row; SCOPE_CONTRACT.md §M2(a), which does not mention sectoral modes.
findings.recommended_revision: Add M2(a3) as a separately challengeable claim: 'That the sectoral family n = m is slowed systematically less than adjacent degrees, that the cause is the single-sided tridiagonal Coriolis coupling at the bottom of the degree ladder, and that this is established causally by basis truncation rather than inferred.' Step 11 must then hunt prior art specifically on the n = m Rossby/Hough class — Longuet-Higgins (1968) discusses the Rossby-Haurwitz class explicitly, and Paldor's work on equatorially confined and zonally propagating modes is the obvious second place to look.

findings.issue: M2(c) bundles three, arguably four, separable things and presupposes a positive outcome the project's own conventions say may not exist. (c1) The Doppler correction c_intrinsic = c_ground - ū: zero novelty, this is a correctness requirement, and standard since Hayashi (1971). (c2) The two-season ENSO-contrast design (DJF 2013/14 neutral vs DJF 2015/16 strong El Niño): a robustness design, not an observational result; separable from (c1) in both directions — you can Doppler-correct one season, or use two seasons uncorrected. (c3) The precondition nobody has committed to: CONVENTIONS states plainly that a resolvable westward branch may not exist at 500 hPa ('plausible, since upper-tropospheric advection is strong enough to sweep all planetary-scale signals eastward') and that a null result must be stated as a finding. (c4) Level selection — 250/300 hPa may have to be tried in addition to 500 hPa. M2(c) is worded as a completed comparison ('That the modelled intrinsic phase speed IS compared against reanalysis'), which makes a contract clause contingent on an empirical outcome. Separately, M2(c) exceeds the blueprint: §10.4 caps the observational comparison at 'order of magnitude and dominant wavenumber' and says explicitly it is 'one of scales, not of trajectories'; CONVENTIONS says the blueprint governs on scientific matters.
findings.evidence: SCOPE_CONTRACT.md §M2(c); docs/CONVENTIONS.md 'Observational comparison: Doppler correction' steps 1-4 and 'Why the two-season design pays for itself here'; PROJECT_BLUEPRINT.md §10.4 and §7.3 'Scope discipline'; PROJECT_BLUEPRINT.md §7.3 request spec, which still says 'One Northern Hemisphere winter season'.
findings.recommended_revision: Replace M2(c) with three clauses. M2(c1): 'That the ground-relative/intrinsic distinction is handled correctly via wavenumber-frequency (Hayashi) decomposition — stated as a methodological correctness requirement grounded in Hayashi (1971, 1979) and Randel & Held (1991), NOT as a contribution.' M2(c2): 'That the comparison is repeated in an ENSO-neutral and a strongly perturbed winter so that agreement is attributable to the beta mechanism rather than to one season's background flow — a robustness design.' M2(c3): 'That the campaign establishes whether a westward-propagating barotropic branch is resolvable at all at 500 hPa, and at which level, with the two-reanalysis (ERA5 vs NCEP/NCAR R1) spread reported as observational uncertainty — a null result being a reportable finding, not a failure.' Also add a line binding M2(c) to blueprint §10.4's order-of-magnitude/dominant-wavenumber cap, or log a blueprint §10.4 revision.

findings.issue: M2(b) is not compound but it is mathematically false as worded, and the error is one a GFD referee will catch in the abstract. 'A sufficient stability test' claims something a normal-mode eigenvalue problem cannot deliver. Finding a growing eigenvalue demonstrates linear modal instability for that base state — fine. Finding NO growing eigenvalue does not prove stability: barotropic shear operators are strongly non-normal, and transient/non-modal growth, the continuous spectrum, and subcritical nonlinear instability all sit outside the modal spectrum. Theory §9.3 compounds this by calling the solid-body-rotation result ('real to machine precision at every m tested') evidence of a 'genuine sufficient computational test'. It is not; it is evidence of modal stability only. The claim costs nothing to fix and, unfixed, hands a referee a free strike on the contribution the project is otherwise most secure about.
findings.evidence: SCOPE_CONTRACT.md §M2(b) heading 'A sufficient stability test, not merely a necessary one'; theory/derivations.tex §9.3 'converts Section 8's necessary condition into a genuine sufficient computational test'; §8.3 'Necessary, not sufficient'.
findings.recommended_revision: Reword M2(b) to: 'A predictive modal stability calculation, where Rayleigh-Kuo gives only a prohibition. That a linear normal-mode eigenvalue problem about each zonal base state returns growth rates σ(m) = m·Im(c_a) and eigenmode structure, with a resolution-doubling spurious-mode filter (N = 240 vs 480), so that the nonlinear runs have a quantitative target. Modal stability is not proved by the absence of growing eigenvalues; non-modal transient growth is outside the scope of this calculation and is stated as such.' Add Farrell & Ioannou (1996) generalised stability theory to the M1/M2(b) grounding list so the limitation is cited rather than merely admitted.

findings.issue: X1 IS secretly load-bearing, and the boundary condition as written misses the load. The stated in-scope remnant — 'enough only to state why this project deliberately stays barotropic' — covers the MODEL-CHOICE defence (theory §1.1, blueprint §2.4), which is already written and already cheap. It does not cover the OBSERVATIONAL defence that M2(c) depends on. CONVENTIONS requires a Hayashi decomposition whose entire stated purpose is to separate 'eastward-propagating baroclinic disturbances — a physically distinct instability mechanism with its own energy source' from any westward barotropic signal. To defend that separation to a referee the paper needs: (i) the observed phase-speed/wavenumber phenomenology of mid-latitude baroclinic eddies at 500 hPa, so a reader can see the branches are separable at all; (ii) the space-time spectral methodology itself; (iii) evidence bearing on whether a westward barotropic branch is detectable at that level. None of that is Eady/Charney/Green model detail, so X1 is nominally satisfied — but the sentence 'Eady/Charney/Green model detail is not needed' will in practice cause the campaign to skip the observational phenomenology, which is the part it actually needs. Blueprint §10.4 makes it worse: it attributes 'disagreement in detail' to 'baroclinicity, vertical structure and forcing absent from the model' — an assertion that itself needs a citation X1 gives no mandate to acquire.
findings.evidence: SCOPE_CONTRACT.md X1 row; docs/CONVENTIONS.md 'Observational comparison: Doppler correction' step 1; PROJECT_BLUEPRINT.md §10.4 final sentence and §7.3 'Scope discipline'; theory/derivations.tex §1.1 (the only place baroclinicity is mentioned, and only to exclude it).
findings.recommended_revision: Rewrite X1's in-scope column: 'Enough to state why this project stays barotropic (model-choice defence), AND — explicitly in scope — the observed phase-speed and wavenumber phenomenology of mid-latitude transient eddies at 500/300/250 hPa, plus wavenumber-frequency spectral methodology, sufficient to defend the separation of the eastward baroclinic branch from any westward barotropic branch. Baroclinic instability THEORY (Eady/Charney/Green model detail, growth-rate scalings, two-layer models) remains out of scope; baroclinic eddy OBSERVATIONS are in scope because M2(c) cannot be defended without them.' Seed the campaign with Hayashi (1971, 1979), Randel & Held (1991, JAS, 500 hPa eddy phase-speed spectra), Blackmon (1976) storm-track spectra, Wheeler & Kiladis (1999).

findings.issue: X3 IS load-bearing, and it collides head-on with exit criterion 3. X3 caps §7 at 'the single Rhines-scale connection already in §7 ... nothing beyond Rhines (1975) and Vallis & Maltrud (1993).' But §7.3 does not merely state the Rhines scale; it makes a comparative-planetology claim: that a factor-4 sweep of L_R is 'the difference between a few broad jets and many narrow ones, which is the difference between a terrestrial banding pattern and a Jovian one', and it states in terms that this 'gives the discussion section somewhere real to go — Jovian banding, slowly rotating worlds.' Neither Rhines (1975) nor Vallis & Maltrud (1993) supports that. Neither is about giant-planet banding, and neither establishes jet NUMBER as a function of L_R on a sphere. Worse, the Rhines scale's status as a jet-spacing predictor is actively contested in the literature a TCFD referee will know — the zonostrophic-regime work distinguishes L_R from L_β and disputes the arrest picture. Exit criterion 3 demands every theory section §1-§12 carry a supporting or motivating citation; X3 guarantees §7 is discharged by two references that motivate the scaling and support none of its stated payoff. Supporting evidence that §7 is not as 'fixed' as the contract's frame asserts: §7.3 attributes the Ω sweep to 'runs P-14 through P-18', but blueprint §8.2 assigns the Ω sweep to P-08 to P-12 (P-14/15 are linearity checks, P-16 meridional structure, P-17 resolution, P-18 hyperdiffusion).
findings.evidence: SCOPE_CONTRACT.md X3 row and exit criterion 3; theory/derivations.tex §7.3 (sec:rhines, 'Consequence for the rotation-rate campaign') including the Jovian sentence and the 'P-14 through P-18' attribution; PROJECT_BLUEPRINT.md §8.2 run table.
findings.recommended_revision: Widen X3's in-scope column: 'The Rhines-scale connection in §7, INCLUDING the planetary-regime interpretation it is used for. In scope: the planetary-jets literature sufficient to support the terrestrial-vs-Jovian banding statement (e.g. Williams 1978; Cho & Polvani 1996; Vasavada & Showman 2005; Huang & Robinson 1998), and the published criticism of the Rhines scale as a jet-spacing predictor (the zonostrophic-regime / L_β-vs-L_R literature — Sukoriansky et al. 2007; Scott & Dritschel). Out of scope: closure schemes, LES, spectral-transfer theory.' Alternatively, if the campaign will not fund that, strike the Jovian sentence from theory §7.3 and demote the payoff to 'slowly and rapidly rotating regimes' with no comparative-planetology claim. Do one or the other; do not leave the claim standing on two references that do not support it. Separately, fix the P-14..P-18 / P-08..P-12 run-ID mismatch, and log it per CONVENTIONS 'Authoritative source'.

findings.issue: X2's boundary condition is the word 'Nothing', which is too absolute to be true. The project's entire Tier 3 observational programme runs on ERA5 — a data-assimilation product of an operational NWP centre — with NCEP/NCAR R1 as fallback. To characterise those as data products, to state what a reanalysis is, and to state the limitation that matters here (the assimilating model shapes the very transient-eddy phase speeds M2(c) will measure, so an apparent westward branch could be a model artefact rather than an observation), the paper must cite reanalysis and data-assimilation methodology. That literature sits inside the NWP box X2 closes. The project already holds Hersbach (2020) and Kalnay (1996), so it will cite them regardless — which means X2 as written is a rule the campaign will silently break rather than a boundary it will hold to.
findings.evidence: SCOPE_CONTRACT.md X2 row; PROJECT_BLUEPRINT.md §7.3 (ERA5 primary, NCEP/NCAR R1 fallback); docs/literature/ contains hersbach_2020_era5_global_reanalysis.pdf and kalnay_1996_ncep_ncar_reanalysis.pdf.
findings.recommended_revision: Rewrite X2's in-scope column: 'No forecasting or forecast-skill claim, and no NWP model-development literature. IN scope: reanalysis and data-assimilation methodology sufficient to (i) characterise ERA5 and NCEP/NCAR R1 as data products and (ii) state the limitation that assimilated transient-eddy phase speeds are partly a property of the assimilating model — a caveat M2(c) must carry.' Cap it at roughly four references so it cannot bleed.

findings.issue: Exit criterion 4 is the clearest judgement call disguised as a threshold in the document. 'Every one of the three contributions has been adversarially challenged and the novelty claim narrowed wherever the challenge succeeded' has no evidentiary bar, no artefact, no adjudicator, and no failure state. It is satisfiable by writing 'we challenged it and it survived.' A criterion that cannot fail is not a criterion. It also miscounts: it says THREE contributions, but F1, F3 and F4 show the contract actually contains five or six separable claims, and a bundled challenge will let the weak fragments ride on the strong ones — which is the precise failure mode M2's own preamble ('stated here in the form it will be challenged') was written to prevent.
findings.evidence: SCOPE_CONTRACT.md exit criterion 4 and §M2 preamble; SCOPE_CONTRACT.md §M3 'The campaign is instructed to try to defeat each of the three claims above (Step 11)'.
findings.recommended_revision: Replace criterion 4 with an artefact-producing version: 'For each claim fragment (a1, a2, a3, b, c1, c2, c3) a row exists in docs/literature/NOVELTY_CHALLENGE.md recording: (i) at least six specific search queries run, verbatim, with dates; (ii) the three nearest prior-art papers found, with full citations, and one sentence each on what that paper already did; (iii) the resulting claim wording after narrowing. Decision rule, applied mechanically: if any single prior paper already reports substantially the same result for substantially the same configuration, the fragment is demoted from "new" to "confirms/extends" in the manuscript, and the demotion is recorded. A fragment with zero nearest-prior-art rows has not been challenged; it has been skipped.'

findings.issue: Exit criterion 3 is checkable but vacuous, because of its own escape hatch. 'has at least one supporting or motivating citation, OR an explicit written statement that it needs none because it is derived internally' can discharge every one of the twelve theory sections by writing one sentence. The project is already leaning on that move: theory §6.1 says outright 'the derivation here does not depend on either [Longuet-Higgins or Swarztrauber], since the validation target is the internal ε→0 limit'; MISSING.md applies the same argument to Haurwitz (1940b) and to both Hough references; §12 discharges H6 as 'numerical, not predicted here'. Each individual use is defensible. The criterion as written places no limit on how many times it can be used, and provides no test of whether the escape was justified. Second defect: 'supporting OR motivating' collapses two very different standards. A motivating citation ('people care about jets') is not evidence; a supporting citation is. The disjunction lets a section with no supporting literature pass on a motivational cite.
findings.evidence: SCOPE_CONTRACT.md exit criterion 3; theory/derivations.tex §6.1; §12 H6 row and closing note; docs/literature/MISSING.md 'Why the project is not blocked' (used three times).
findings.recommended_revision: Tighten criterion 3 to: 'Every hypothesis H1-H10 and every theory section §1-§12 has at least one SUPPORTING citation (evidence for a stated result), recorded separately from any merely motivating citation. A section may instead be discharged as internally derived only if the written statement ALSO (i) names the closest external result it could have been checked against, with a full citation, and (ii) states why that check was not or could not be performed. At most three sections may be discharged this way; a fourth triggers a review of whether the campaign under-retrieved.' The (i)/(ii) template is exactly what MISSING.md already does well for the Hough references — make it the standard rather than an ad hoc good deed.

findings.issue: Exit criteria 1 and 2 under-specify verification in two ways the project has already been burned by. (i) 'confirmed to resolve during this session' proves an identifier exists; it does not prove the identifier is the right one for the recorded title/authors/year/pages. The project has already made exactly this error at the file level: MISSING.md records that haurwitz_1940_motion_of_atmospheric_disturbances.pdf was NOT Haurwitz (1940b) but Haurwitz (1940a), J. Mar. Res. 3(1) 35-50 — a resolving, plausible, wrong attribution caught only in L3-PATCH. Resolution is not identity. (ii) Criterion 2 conflates 'identifier verified' with 'source read'. MISSING.md holds Longuet-Higgins (1968) and Swarztrauber & Kasahara (1985) as DOI-confirmed but full-text-unobtained — and theory §6.1 already cites both for 'the classical formulation and its eigenstructure'. That is a citation to a paper nobody on the project has read, which is a softer version of the exact failure the paper-trail rule was written to stop ('a value stated from familiarity rather than from a source'). Criterion 2 as worded neither forbids it nor requires it to be recorded. (iii) Minor but real: '≥ 60 verified references' has no relevance gate, so it can be satisfied by padding — which pushes directly against M3's narrowing discipline and against X1-X4.
findings.evidence: SCOPE_CONTRACT.md exit criteria 1 and 2, and 'The paper trail rule'; docs/literature/MISSING.md — the *Note* on the Haurwitz 1940a/1940b misidentification, and the 'Genuinely unobtainable' table; theory/derivations.tex §6.1 citing longuethiggins1968 and swarztrauber1985.
findings.recommended_revision: Criterion 1: append 'and, for each, the resolved landing page's metadata (title, first author, year, volume, page range) is confirmed to match the recorded entry. A DOI that resolves to a different paper is an unverified reference, not a verified one.' Add a relevance gate: 'and every row names its target — a hypothesis ID, a theory section, or a claim fragment. A reference with no named target does not count toward the 60.' Criterion 2: add a third state — 'Every pool row is marked verified-and-read or verified-unread. A verified-unread source may be cited for historical attribution only, never as evidence for a technical statement; theory §6.1's citation of Longuet-Higgins (1968) and Swarztrauber & Kasahara (1985) must be reworded to attribution-only or the sources obtained.'

findings.issue: No exit criterion checks M1 at all. The four criteria cover reference count (1), reference quality (2), hypothesis and theory-section coverage (3), and contribution challenge (4). M1 — grounding the claim that material PV conservation is the common source of both Rossby-wave dispersion and barotropic instability, along the named line Rossby (1939) / Haurwitz (1940b) / Kuo (1949) / Hoskins, McIntyre & Robertson (1985) / Bretherton (1966) / Heifetz, Bishop & Alpert (1999) — is checked by nothing. That is the one thing the campaign cannot afford to leave unchecked, because CONVENTIONS names the unification statement as the sentence the entire manuscript is organised around. Criterion 3 is adjacent (it covers theory sections) but not equivalent: a per-section citation sweep does not test whether the CROSS-section thesis is grounded.
findings.evidence: SCOPE_CONTRACT.md §M1 and exit criteria 1-4; docs/CONVENTIONS.md 'Theoretical framework: the spine' — 'whose closing statement is the sentence the manuscript is organised around'; theory/derivations.tex §10.4 'The identification'.
findings.recommended_revision: Add exit criterion 5: 'M1 is discharged: every one of the six named anchors (Rossby 1939; Haurwitz 1940b; Kuo 1949; Bretherton 1966; Hoskins, McIntyre & Robertson 1985; Heifetz, Bishop & Alpert 1999) is verified and held, or its non-holding is recorded in MISSING.md with the substitute actually used; and the one-interface/two-interface identification of theory §10.4 has been checked against prior statements of the same unification, with the nearest three recorded.'

findings.issue: Claim (a) is nowhere near narrow enough. A GFD referee names the prior art before finishing the abstract, and the contract's own supporting documents show the project knows it. The departure of divergent (Hough) eigenfrequencies from the nondivergent Rossby-Haurwitz speed as a function of Lamb's parameter is not a gap in the literature — it IS the classical Hough-mode literature. Longuet-Higgins (1968) computed and tabulated the eigenfrequencies of Laplace's tidal equations over the full ε range including the Rossby-Haurwitz class; Swarztrauber & Kasahara (1985) solved precisely the vector-harmonic form of eq. (eq:houghevp); Kasahara (1976) is open-access and covers the same normal modes; Hough functions are computed routinely today in normal-mode-function decomposition packages. Claiming 'quantification of the departure' while holding neither of the two canonical references (MISSING.md) is the highest-risk sentence in the contract. What survives narrowing is not the quantification but the sectoral-family result of F3.
findings.evidence: SCOPE_CONTRACT.md §M2(a); docs/literature/MISSING.md 'Genuinely unobtainable' and 'Accessible substitutes to obtain'; theory/derivations.tex §6.1 (which itself attributes 'the classical formulation and its eigenstructure' to Longuet-Higgins 1968 and Swarztrauber & Kasahara 1985) and §6.4.
findings.recommended_revision: Give Step 11 a named dig list for (a) and require each to be resolved before the gap statement is written: Longuet-Higgins (1968); Kasahara (1976) [open access — obtain]; Swarztrauber & Kasahara (1985); Hoskins (1973) 'Stability of the Rossby-Haurwitz wave' QJRMS [relevant to both (a) and (b)]; Thuburn & Li (2000) [already held — read it for what it says about RH waves in the divergent SWE]; Paldor (2015); the normal-mode-function / MODES literature (Žagar et al.) for modern Hough computation. Then reword M2(a1) to the narrow survivable form: 'the departure is recomputed at this project's own resolution and parameters as a cross-check, and the new content is the sectoral-family exception and its structural cause' — not 'the departure is quantified'.

findings.issue: Claim (b) is not narrow enough either, on the method axis. Normal-mode barotropic stability eigenvalue problems for zonal flows on a sphere, expanded in associated Legendre functions of fixed order m with a generalised eigenvalue solve, are decades old and were standard well before spectral codes were cheap. The 'gap left by the Rayleigh-Kuo criterion' has been closed repeatedly since the 1970s; what the project has is an execution of that standard calculation for ITS base states, which is a legitimate but much smaller claim. The single most dangerous specific hit: the Galewsky, Scott & Polvani (2004) jet is one of the most-used test cases in the spherical shallow-water literature, and if anyone has already published a normal-mode growth-rate spectrum for it, theory §9.3's headline (σ = 2.07e-5 s⁻¹, m* ≈ 6, e-folding 0.56 days, resolved band 1 ≤ m ≤ 8) becomes a reproduction rather than a result. That must be searched in Step 11, not discovered in review.
findings.evidence: SCOPE_CONTRACT.md §M2(b); theory/derivations.tex §9.1-§9.3, particularly the spherical-harmonic expansion eq. (eq:expansion) and eq. (eq:galewskygrowth); docs/CONVENTIONS.md 'Authorised extensions', Extension C justification; PROJECT_BLUEPRINT.md §2.3 'The contribution is not new theory.'
findings.recommended_revision: Named dig list for (b), to be exhausted before the gap statement: Kuo (1949); Hoskins (1973); Baines (1976) 'The stability of planetary waves on a sphere' JFM; Frederiksen (barotropic instability of zonal flows on a sphere, late 1970s-early 1980s); Simmons, Wallace & Branstator (1983); Ishioka & Yoden; Thuburn & Li (2000) [held]; and an explicit targeted search on 'Galewsky jet linear stability / normal mode / growth rate / eigenvalue' plus a forward-citation sweep of Galewsky et al. (2004). Narrow M2(b) in advance to the execution claim: 'growth rates and eigenmode structure for the specific base states of this campaign, with a stated spurious-mode filter, reported so the nonlinear runs have a quantitative target' — and let the CRW identification, not the EVP, carry the physics.

findings.issue: The structural problem underneath all of Q4: none of (a), (b), (c) is the paper's actual organising claim, and the contract has classified the paper's thesis as background. CONVENTIONS states the manuscript is organised around 'the wave-propagation mechanism and the instability mechanism are the same physics, viewed as one interface versus two' (theory §10.4), and §10 is called 'the physical heart of the argument'. The contract puts that under M1 — the list of things to be GROUNDED in prior work — and puts three much smaller items under M2 as the contributions. If a referee accepts M1 as established (it is: Hoskins, McIntyre & Robertson 1985 and Heifetz, Bishop & Alpert 1999 are named in M1 itself), the paper is left claiming a re-quantification (a), a standard calculation (b), and a hygiene correction (c). Blueprint §2.3 already says so in plain words — 'The contribution is not new theory' — and locates the contribution in controlled verified isolation of the beta-effect across the wave-to-instability regime with quantified uncertainty. M2 is out of step with the project's own honest self-assessment, in the direction of overclaiming.
findings.evidence: SCOPE_CONTRACT.md §M1 vs §M2; docs/CONVENTIONS.md 'Theoretical framework: the spine'; theory/derivations.tex §10 preamble and §10.4 'The identification'; PROJECT_BLUEPRINT.md §2.3.
findings.recommended_revision: Choose one and write it down. EITHER promote the one-interface/two-interface identification to M2(d) and challenge it in Step 11 like the rest — nearest prior art to dig: Bretherton (1966), Hoskins/McIntyre/Robertson (1985), Baines & Mitsudera (1994), Heifetz/Bishop/Alpert (1999), Harnik & Heifetz (2007), Carpenter et al. (2013); it will not survive as new physics but it can survive as a coherent single-mechanism exposition on the sphere — OR rewrite M3 to say explicitly what blueprint §2.3 already says: 'the contribution is verified, uncertainty-quantified execution across the wave-to-instability regime in one consistent framework, plus a single-mechanism physical narrative; (a)-(c) are supporting results, not independent novelty claims.' Leaving M2 as three standalone 'claimed contributions' is the version most likely to draw a hostile report.

summary: The contract is well-built as a process document — the paper-trail rule and the zero-unverifiable-references rule are stronger than most projects manage — but its scientific core is unsound in three ways. M2(a) and M2(c) are each two or three separable claims bundled so that the weak fragments ride on the strong ones, and the strongest genuinely new result in the theory (the sectoral n=m exception, theory §6.5, with its causal basis-deletion test) is not named in the contract at all; meanwhile the ε→0 'internal validation target' is fitted over ε ≤ 1e-2, decouples the very Coriolis matrix that produces the departure, and cannot validate the 40% slowing quoted at ε ≈ 8.80. Two exclusions are load-bearing: X1 as worded blocks the observed baroclinic-eddy phenomenology that M2(c)'s Hayashi branch separation depends on, and X3's two-reference cap cannot support theory §7.3's Jovian-banding payoff, colliding directly with exit criterion 3. Exit criteria 3 and 4 are the weakest clauses — criterion 3 is dischargeable by writing 'derived internally' twelve times, criterion 4 has no artefact and no failure state — and on novelty, all three claims as worded name their own prior art: Longuet-Higgins/Kasahara/Swarztrauber for (a), the 1970s spherical barotropic-stability literature plus any existing normal-mode analysis of the Galewsky jet for (b), and Hayashi/Randel & Held for (c). Blueprint §2.3 already says 'the contribution is not new theory'; M2 should be brought back into line with that before Step 11 spends a campaign defending claims the project does not need to make.
